bib.title: A Survey of Self-Evolving Agents: What, When, How, and Where to Evolve on the Path to Artificial Super Intelligence

read.skipped: Reference list (after about char 262,681) was skimmed by grep for lineage ids only; there is no appendix.

question: How can the field of self-evolving LLM agents be organised around what, when and how agents evolve, and how should such agents be evaluated and made safe?
contributions: We establish a unified theoretical framework for characterizing self-evolutionary processes in agent systems, anchored around three fundamental dimensions: what evolves, how it evolves, and when it evolves, providing clear design guidance for future self-evolving agentic systems.

We further investigate the evaluation benchmark or environment tailored for self-evolving agents, highlighting emerging metrics and challenges related to adaptability, robustness, and real-world complexity.

We showcase several key real-world applications across various domains, including autonomous software engineering, personalized education, healthcare, and intelligent virtual assistance, illustrating the practical potential of self-evolving agents.
We identify critical open challenges and promising future research directions, emphasizing aspects like safety, personalization, multi-agent co-evolution, and scalability.

results.claim: Most existing benchmarks reset agent state between tasks, so they cannot measure accumulation or degradation of knowledge.
results.setup: Survey's review of retention-oriented benchmarks (LifelongAgentBench, LTMBenchmark, MemoryAgentBench); an assessment, not a counted statistic.
results.quote: the overwhelming majority of existing benchmarks adopt episodic evaluation where agent state resets between tasks, fundamentally precluding measurement of knowledge accumulation or degradation

results.claim: Deployment checklist includes a pre-update safety validation of a self-modified model against a golden dataset of safety-critical prompts.
results.setup: Table 12, category Self-Modification Control; applies to a self-modified model before deployment, aimed at catastrophic forgetting of alignment. Synthesised by the authors from cited guardrail work, not tested.
results.quote: Before a self-modified model is deployed, it is automatically evaluated against a "golden dataset" of safety-critical prompts to prevent catastrophic forgetting of alignment.

results.claim: Any self-modification needs an audit trail and rollback to a known safe state.
results.setup: Sec 8.3.2 prescriptive guardrails; recommendation, no experiment.
results.quote: Any self-modification must be accompanied by a comprehensive audit trail. This ensures that changes are traceable and reversible.
results.note: Table 12 lists these as Immutable Audit Trail (logged with trigger, changes made, outcome), Version Control for Safe States, and a Tested Rollback Mechanism that is one-click and regularly tested.

results.claim: Self-training on agent-generated data can erase safety alignment (misevolution).

results.claim: EvoAgent overall success on 67 Minecraft tasks improves from 21.80% to 30.29%.
results.setup: Worked example in Table 10 for long-horizon protocol; the survey notes EvoAgent leaves retention (BWT/FGT), CPG and safety-drift unreported.
results.quote: Overall SR improves from 21.80% to 30.29% (relative gain ≈105.9%).
results.note: The stated 105.9% relative gain does not equal (30.29-21.80)/21.80, which is about 39%; it likely refers to a different tier or baseline. The survey does not explain it.

limits: A survey with no experiments of its own; every performance number is second-hand and drawn from different setups.

The authors call it a guiding synthesis because conceptual boundaries are still being negotiated, and say fully autonomous self-evolution without human intervention is an aspirational goal rather than the current norm.
Table 11 is an illustrative snapshot; latency, cost and safety are not consistently reported.
The guardrail checklist (Table 12) is a synthesis of recommendations and is not validated empirically.
Covers work up to about late 2025 (v4 dated 16 Jan 2026).
Says nothing about review cadence, a 'no change needed' outcome, or busywork edits in an evolve loop.
practices: Log every self-modification (model weights, memory, toolset, core logic) with trigger, change and outcome in an immutable audit trail (Table 12).
Version agent state and tag known safe versions; keep a one-click rollback that is regularly tested (Table 12).
Validate a self-modified model against a golden dataset of safety-critical prompts before deploying it (Table 12).
Monitor for reward hacking and alert on sharp unexplained metric changes (Table 12).
Require human review for any change to the agent's own goals or safety constraints, and human approval gates for high-stakes actions (Table 12, Sec 8.3.2).
Run continuous monitoring and red-teaming for long-horizon drift, since static pre-deployment safety evaluation is insufficient (Sec 8.3.2).
Execute agent-created tools in a sandbox and run static analysis and vulnerability scanning before integrating them (Sec 8.3.2, Table 12).
Report whether evolution strategies and task sequences are predetermined, procedurally sampled or agent-generated; the feedback source; and the frequency of external interventions (Sec 7.1.6).

For long-horizon evaluation, assume full state persistence, set stage and cumulative evolution budgets (K_stage, K_total) and log scheduled retention probes and evolution decision logs (Sec 7.2.4, Table 10).

terms.definition: the agent that modifies its internal parameters, contextual state, toolset, or architectural topology based on its own trajectories or feedback signals, with the explicit objective of improving future performance.
adaptive processes that occur during task execution, where agents recognize their limitations on a specific problem and initiate targeted learning mechanisms
learning processes that occur between task completions, leveraging accumulated experiences to improve future performance
average accuracy drop on old tasks after an agent learns a new one; FGT_t = 1/(t-1) * sum_i [max_j J_ij - J_it]
average accuracy improvement on old tasks due to experience from new tasks; BWT_t = 1/(t-1) * sum_i (J_it - J_ii)
CPG_t = Total Cost_t / (Performance Gain_t + epsilon); lower is more efficient learning
an initially aligned agent discovers that misaligned behaviors are more rewarding, causing its policy to "tip" and abandon its initial constraints

figures.caption: Taxonomy of self-evolving agents, in which agents are analyzed along the what, when, how, and where dimensions, with selected representative methods and systems annotated at each leaf node.
figures.why: Index of methods by what, when, how and where.

figures.caption: An overview of when to evolve. The top pathway illustrates intra-test-time self-evolution, where adaptation (e.g., variant generation, verification, and policy update) occurs within task execution. The bottom pathway depicts inter-test-time self-evolution, where learning happens retrospectively through rollout, trajectory analysis, and policy updates.
figures.why: Shows the fast in-task loop against the slower between-task loop.

figures.caption: Standardized evaluation protocols
figures.why: Side-by-side short-horizon and long-horizon protocol requirements for persistence, budgets and logging.

figures.caption: Compliance checklist for deploying self-evolving agents
figures.why: The guardrail checklist in one place.
